study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Perception of length of pre-hospital labor
outcome: Obstetrical interventions (continuous electronic fetal monitoring, augmentation of labor, use of narcotic, epidural analgesia)
cohort: 1247 healthy nulliparous women in spontaneous labor at term with a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation
finding: Women who reported being in labor for 24 hours or longer upon hospital admission had a higher risk of cesarean birth and more obstetrical interventions.
